climate.koppen_name: Cold, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Riesling, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.

soil.rock: Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it. Sandstone is sand bound into rock. It weathers to light, sandy soil that drains freely. Marl is a limy clay. It holds water and makes vines ripen later, which keeps acidity in the grapes.
soil.top: The topsoil stores water through dry spells, but stays wet and cold after rain, which slows ripening and can swell the grapes. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 2°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
